newsitem.title: UK: British archbishop extends hand to Hindus.
newsitem.headline: British archbishop extends hand to Hindus.

text.p: Britain's Archbishop of Canterbury visited the largest Hindu temple outside of India on Friday, urging Christians and Hindus to join forces in the fight against racism.
Dr George Carey, head of the Anglican church, has toured scores of mosques, synagogues and shrines over the years but it was his first visit to the towering temple in north London.

"Building on a foundation of our common humanity, our shared spiritual quest and our common longings for peace, acceptance and love, we can speak and act together in a number of ways," he told the congregation.

"For instance, we can together stand against the evils of racism; we can together challenge the materialism that threatens to become all-enveloping; we can together work for the protection and enhancement of our environment; we can together bring practical help and support to those who suffer, both in this country and around the world."
The temple, an architectural gem in the drab London suburb of Neasden, has drawn 800,000 people in its first year, half of them non-Hindu.
A church official said Carey wanted to use his trip to foster good relations with other faiths.
Chief priest Atma Swarup Swami said: "It is indeed a great step towards better inter-religious understanding."
